title: AI Search Analytics Confirm Higher Ed's LLM Winners Are Large Publics/Nonprofits

excerpt: Summary - What Do AI Search Analytics Tools Tell Us About Online Higher Ed? For the past year, I’ve been writing about how AI engines disproportionately recommend large public and nonprofit universities over competitors, including the publicly traded, for-profit education companies I track. Until recently, the evidence consisted largely of anecdotal, unscientific exercises examining LLM responses, along with commentary from management teams about the impact of AI search on student acquisition. A growing category of AI search analytics companies now allows us to examine these questions more systematically. At a reasonable price point, accessible even to the layperson. I used Otterly.ai to evaluate more than 30 unbranded search prompts across multiple AI engines. The platform measures how frequently university brands appear in AI-generated responses, where the brands are positioned within answers, and which websites the engines cite as sources. The output from Otterly.ai supports the following conclusions. - New analytics allow stakeholders and leadership teams to measure AI visibility rather than relying on anecdotes found in annual reports and/or earnings commentary. Institutions need to start using AI engine marketing metrics to describe their success, or lack thereof. - Public and nonprofit universities dominate AI recommendations. The institutions with the highest brand coverage in a sample of online institutions were all public or nonprofit universities. - AI recommendations are highly concentrated among a handful of institutions. Western Governors University (WGU) and Southern New Hampshire University (SNHU) account for half of the share of voice. These two brands also appear earlier in AI-generated answers than their competitors. - Third-party education websites with relatively low site traffic play a surprisingly prominent role as the source for AI-generated answers.
